extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, USPTO officials, policymakers, and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes statutory and procedural standards introduced or amended by the patent reform legislation (e.g., inter partes/inter partes review, post-grant review, fee-setting, marking, supplemental examination), intended to guide practice, USPTO procedure, and litigation. Useful as a checklist of new/changed legal and procedural requirements practitioners and policymakers must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent-owner written statements in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Expands documents that may be cited in a reexamination proceeding to include written statements of the patent owner that have been filed in a proceeding before a Federal court or the USPTO regarding the scope of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These written statements (documents, pleadings, evidence) shall be considered only to determine the proper meaning of the claims that are the subject of the request in a proceeding and are not intended to be a basis for institution of a reexamination proceeding; intended to prevent patent owners from offering differing interpretations of prior art in different proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for reexamination limited to patents or printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexaminations will continue to be available only on the basis of 'patents or printed publications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of 'patent and printed publication' prior art in the amended section 301 is intended to be coextensive with these terms in current section 102 of title 35; other amendments are not intended to change this sole basis for initiating reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends the ex parte reexamination procedure to allow the Director to institute a reexamination on the Director's own initiative if a substantial new question of patentability is raised by patents or publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the Director authority to act sua sponte when patents/publications raise substantial new questions of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to inter partes review and elevated institution threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts inter partes reexamination to an adjudicative proceeding renamed 'inter partes review' and raises the threshold for instituting review from 'significant new question of patentability' to 'reasonable likelihood of success.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfaction of the new threshold is assessed based on information presented both in the petition and in the patent owner's response; intended to reduce the high grant rate under the prior lower threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel standard in inter partes review ('reasonably could have raised')
rubrics_metrics.description: A party that uses inter partes review is estopped from raising in a subsequent PTO proceeding any issue that it raised or reasonably could have raised in the inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to subsequent administrative proceedings (e.g., ex parte reexam or later inter partes review) to prevent re-litigation of issues that were or could have been raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of pre-1999 challenge limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeals the 1999 limit on challenging patents in inter partes reexamination; all patents can be challenged in inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes prior temporal restriction so patents issued before 1999 are no longer categorically excluded from inter partes review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in inter partes review (preponderance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners bear the burden of proving that a patent is invalid by a preponderance of the evidence in inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the evidentiary standard for inter partes review adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-month filing limit for using inter partes review during litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties who want to use inter partes review during litigation must seek a proceeding within 12 months of being served with a complaint alleging infringement; barred from seeking or maintaining inter partes review if they file a declaratory judgment action that the patent is invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a timing limitation to coordinate administrative review with civil litigation and prevent strategic delays or duplicative actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery in inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may depose witnesses submitting affidavits or declarations and seek such discovery as the Patent Office determines is otherwise necessary in the interest of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited discovery rights in administrative proceedings, subject to Patent Office determination of necessity and interest of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory time-to-decision (12- to 18-month deadline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review must be completed within 1 year of institution, except that the Office can extend this deadline by 6 months for good cause (yielding up to 18 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to provide timely resolution of administrative review; extension authority is narrow and for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oral hearing in inter partes review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party has the right to request an oral hearing as part of an inter partes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows oral argument before the reviewing panel when requested by a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-judge panel and appeal route
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reviews will be conducted before a panel of three Administrative Patent Judges (APJs); decisions will be appealed directly to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes panel composition and directs appellate review to the Federal Circuit for consistency with other patent appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review (time-limited, broad grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a post-grant opposition procedure usable during the first 12 months after grant (or reissue) permitting challenge on any ground related to invalidity under section 282.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to enable early, comprehensive challenges to patent validity while protecting inventors; provides clear procedures for submission of art; ensures the process is time-limited to preserve quiet title for patent owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion rules for post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners, real parties in interest, and their privies are precluded from improperly mounting multiple challenges to a patent or initiating challenges after filing a civil action challenging validity; a final decision prevents challenging any claim on a ground raised in the post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality and estoppel principles prevent re-raising grounds that were or could have been litigated in the post-grant review; filing/instituting post-grant review does not limit patent owners' enforcement avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preissuance third-party submissions (with explanations)
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, third parties may submit prior art and are permitted to make statements concerning the relevance of patents, patent applications, and other printed publications brought to the USPTO's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces prior rule (35 C.F.R. §1.99(d)) that barred any explanation; intended to increase the value of third-party submissions to examiners and encourage submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue clarification for suits against the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that venue for litigation against the USPTO is the district where the USPTO resides (currently the Eastern District of Virginia), and updates statutory sections to reflect that change uniformly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects inadvertent inconsistencies that previously allowed some suits in the District of Columbia.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO fee-setting authority with oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows the USPTO to set or adjust all of its fees so long as they reasonably compensate for services performed; Director must give notice to, and receive input from, the Patent or Trademark Public Advisory Committee (PPAC/TPAC) and follow procedures before prescribing fees by rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed fee changes must be published in the Federal Register with specific rationale and receive at least 45 days of public comment; Director must notify Congress of final decisions and Congress has 45 days to consider; fee changes cannot be effective before the 45-day congressional period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro-entity fee status
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines a 'micro-entity' — a group smaller than current small business entities (truly independent inventors) — to receive tailored fee accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects the USPTO will make accommodations recognizing the special status of micro-entities to nurture innovation among very small inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination to address inequitable conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes supplemental examination of a patent to present information that was not considered, was inadequately considered, or was incorrect in the original prosecution; if the Office determines the information does not present a substantial new question of patentability or the patent remains valid, that information cannot later be used to hold the patent unenforceable or invalid on the basis of inequitable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to reduce reliance on the subjective inequitable conduct doctrine by allowing correction of prosecution record without creating later unenforceability exposure when the Office finds no substantial new question of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: GOCO funding agreement royalty-share adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifies the 1984 GOCO rule so that instead of reimbursing 75% of excess royalties to the Government, the GOCO will retain 85% for further R&D and reimburse the Government 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to reduce disincentives for commercialization by universities and small businesses operating under GOCO provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-strategy patents treated as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandates that tax strategies are 'insufficient to differentiate a claimed invention from the prior art' (i.e., future tax strategies will be considered indistinguishable from publicly available information relevant to claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exclusion is made for software that enables filing returns or assists with finances, but the exclusion does not apply to the tax-strategy-related parts of such software; aims to keep tax-law interpretation and strategy in public domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of best mode as defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends Sec. 282(b) to eliminate as a defense to patent infringement the patentee's failure to comply with the best mode requirement of Sec. 112; other Sec. 112 requirements (written description, enablement) remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responds to concerns that best mode is subjective and of limited relevance in litigation; removes best mode as basis for invalidity or unenforceability, but does not affect other defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual marking permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows patent holders to 'virtually mark' a product by providing the address of a publicly available website that associates the patented article with the patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden remains on the patent holder to demonstrate that the marking was effective; intended to lower marking costs (especially for products where marking is expensive) and facilitate marking of smaller products.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking remedy reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaces the qui tam remedy for false marking with a new action allowing a party that has suffered a competitive injury to seek compensatory damages; the United States may seek the statutory fine ($500 per article), while unrelated private qui tam suits are eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response to surge in false-marking litigation alleging expired/invalid patents; aims to curb opportunistic suits by unrelated private parties and focus relief on actual competitive injuries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice-of-counsel protection (section 298)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bars courts and juries from drawing an adverse inference from an accused infringer's failure to obtain an opinion of counsel about infringement or from his failure to waive privilege and disclose such an opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to protect attorney-client privilege and reduce coercion to obtain or disclose opinions for litigation; applies to findings of both willfulness and intent to induce infringement and legislatively abrogates Broadcom v. Qualcomm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional program for covered business method patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a provisional post-grant proceeding (transitional program) for review of covered business method patents, starting one year after enactment; petitions will not be granted unless the petitioner is first sued for infringement or accused, and the program generally functions on the same terms as other post-grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows stay of civil action if related post-grant proceeding granted; sunsets after 10 years to prevent indefinite avoidance of litigation by relying on the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: District court and Federal Circuit jurisdiction clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that U.S. district courts have original jurisdiction to hear patent cases and that the Federal Circuit has jurisdiction over appeals involving compulsory patent counterclaims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reaffirms and resolves jurisdictional questions raised by prior Supreme Court decision (Holmes Group) to ensure Federal Circuit appellate review where compulsory counterclaims are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on joinder of defendants (Sec. 299)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits joinder: defendants may be joined as defendants or counterclaim defendants only if (1) relief is asserted against the parties arising out of the same transaction regarding the manufacture, use, or importation of the accused product or process, and (2) questions of fact common to all defendants will arise; joinder is not available if based solely on allegations that a defendant has infringed the patent(s) in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislatively abrogates some courts' broader joinder constructions (e.g., E.D. Tex. cases) to prevent mass-joinder of loosely related defendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and pay authority for administrative judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the USPTO Director to expend funds to cover subsistence and travel expenses of non-Federal employees who attend international/domestic IP programs and clarifies the Director may fix pay for Administrative Patent Judges and Administrative Trademark Judges under the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies administrative funding authority for outreach and compensation arrangements under the reorganized Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO revolving fund and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a USPTO revolving fund within the Treasury allowing the agency to keep all fee-generated revenue until expended; requires the Director to submit an annual spending plan and an annual year-end report to the House and Senate Appropriations and Judiciary Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to prevent diversion of fee revenue and enable more efficient agency operations; increases transparency and Congressional oversight via reports and spending plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite office expansion and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires the Director to establish three additional satellite offices within three years (subject to available resources) and includes criteria to be used when selecting new sites; designates the Detroit satellite office as the 'Elijah J. McCoy United States Patent and Trademark Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot (Detroit) already underway; statute provides selection criteria and a naming provision recognizing inventor Elijah J. McCoy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Ombudsman Program for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires the USPTO Director to establish a Patent Ombudsman Program to provide support and services regarding patent filings to small business concerns, subject to available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to assist small businesses navigating patent filings and prosecution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority examination for technologies important to competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits the USPTO to promulgate regulations to prioritize examination of applications for products, processes, or technologies important to the national economy or national competitiveness, without recovering aggregate extra costs of prioritization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows expedited handling of strategically important technologies even if prioritization costs are not fully recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business-day calculation for patent-term-extension deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that the USPTO should apply a 'business-day' construction when calculating the 60-day period for submission related to patent term extension under Sec. 156.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide consistent counting rules aligned with recent case law (e.g., The Medicines Co. v. Kappos).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on implementation of the legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires the USPTO Director to conduct a study regarding implementation of the legislation and other aspects of federal patent policies and practices (patent rights, innovation, competitiveness, small business access to capital), to be completed within 4 years and submitted to the House and Senate Judiciary Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has discretion to examine additional relevant issues; provides a mechanism for evaluating the law's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro bono program for under-resourced inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires the USPTO Director to support intellectual property law associations to establish pro bono programs to assist under-resourced independent inventors and businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges the importance of independent inventors and small businesses and seeks to expand access to patent assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the provisions of the bill take effect one year following the date of enactment and apply to any patent issued on or after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default timing of statutory changes; some provisions may specify alternative effective dates.
